level.title: A2 Elementary Urdu
goals: Handle routine health, school, workplace, and home interactions.
Use polite commands, linked actions, and progressive descriptions.
Participate respectfully in everyday community conversations.

lessons.title: Health and the Clinic
lessons.learn: Describe common symptoms, ask for a doctor, and understand gentle health advice. Use respectful request forms so the same lesson is safe and useful for children, adults, and elders.

grammar.title: Experiencer with مجھے
grammar.explain: Urdu often expresses physical states with مجھے (mujhe, “to me”) plus a noun or sensation and ہے (hai).
mistakes: Do not copy English “I have” word for word; health states commonly use مجھے.

lessons.title: Office Communication
lessons.learn: Handle simple workplace needs: meetings, documents, leave, and courteous instructions. Focus on complete phrases that can be reused without sounding abrupt.

grammar.title: Polite instructions
grammar.explain: Use a respectful imperative ending such as کیجیے, بھیجیے, or آئیے with colleagues, customers, and elders.
mistakes: Avoid a bare familiar command in a formal workplace interaction.

lessons.title: School and Learning
lessons.learn: Follow classroom instructions, ask for clarification, and discuss study. Respectful imperatives ending in ـیے are central to teacher–learner communication.

grammar.title: Respectful classroom imperatives
grammar.explain: Many respectful commands use ـیے. Learn the whole spoken form because spelling changes with different verb stems.
mistakes: Do not attach one ending mechanically without checking the conventional verb form.

lessons.title: Weather and Seasons
lessons.learn: Discuss current weather, seasons, and plans affected by rain or heat. Practise feminine agreement with بارش and گرمی in complete sentences.

grammar.title: Progressive weather statements
grammar.explain: Use a noun plus ہو رہا/رہی ہے for an event in progress. The participle agrees with the grammatical gender of the event noun.
mistakes: Use رہی with feminine بارش and ہوا, not رہا.

grammar.title: sequencing with پہلے / پھر
grammar.explain: Use پہلے and پھر to present steps in order. A brief update is easier to follow when the next action is explicit.

grammar.title: Linked actions with کر
grammar.explain: A completed action can be linked to the next action with the verb stem plus کر (kar), similar to “having done.”

examples.en: Close the door and then sleep.

mistakes: Do not give both linked verbs full tense endings; the final verb carries the main tense or command.

lessons.title: Community Celebrations
lessons.learn: Offer greetings, invite guests, and participate respectfully in community celebrations. The lesson teaches inclusive social language and does not assume the learner’s faith.

grammar.title: Invitations with آئیے
grammar.explain: Use آئیے (aiye) to invite respectfully and کو (ko) to mark a time or recipient. مبارک (mubarak) forms warm greetings.

examples.en: Please give sweets to the children.

mistakes: Match a greeting to the person and occasion; do not assume every listener celebrates the same festival.

culture.text: Urdu distinguishes familiar and respectful address. آپ is widely used for polite address and normally takes honorific agreement; تم is more familiar, but the choice depends on relationship, setting and local practice. A learner should not copy one address form into every conversation.

reading.text: کل عائشہ نے کلینک کو فون کیا۔ اس نے ڈاکٹر سے وقت مانگا اور اپنی علامات بتائیں۔ استقبالیہ نے جمعرات کا وقت دیا۔ عائشہ نے وقت لکھ لیا اور پوچھا کہ رپورٹ ساتھ لانی ہے یا نہیں۔
reading.gloss: Yesterday Ayesha called the clinic. She asked the doctor for an appointment and described her symptoms. Reception gave her a Thursday appointment. Ayesha wrote down the time and asked whether she should bring the report.

listening.script:
عائشہ: کیا جمعرات کو ڈاکٹر سے مل سکتی ہوں؟
استقبالیہ: جی، دس بجے ایک وقت خالی ہے۔
عائشہ: شکریہ، میں رپورٹ بھی لے آؤں گی۔
استقبالیہ: براہ کرم اپنا نام لکھوا دیجیے۔
listening.gloss: Ayesha: Can I see the doctor on Thursday? Reception: Yes, there is an opening at ten. Ayesha: Thank you, I will bring the report too. Reception: Please give us your name.

idioms.meaning: for a plan to work out

mistakes.right: میں نے ڈاکٹر سے وقت پوچھا۔
mistakes.why: Use سے for asking a person; past transitive Urdu commonly marks the subject with نے.
A future-time plan needs a future form, with agreement to the speaker described.
Urdu uses the natural collocation دوا لینا for taking medicine.
